notes.title: DevLog: Dealer, how to deal?
notes.notes:
Yo, so what’s the deal? Or, how do you deal?

In DDS2, dear Dealers, you will become a[b] true person of business[/b]. And, as a person of business, you will need to set meetings with your clientele. To do this, use your trusty early 2000s phone. You know, this indestructible little brick that’s eternally burned into your memory if you ever had one. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43095044/4035b7820e94bf761b0c58c85f266f3e9ceccb7c.jpg[/img]

You can meet your clients between 9 AM and 8 PM. If you respond to their messages quickly, you will earn more reputation, but if you ignore them, you will lose reputation. JUST LIKE IN REAL LIFE.

Reputation is generally a thing you should care about. If you are slow or don’t deliver at all, you’ll lose clients. [b]You can’t run a business without clients![/b] 

On the other hand, if you take care of them, and maybe give them something extra, then they’re going to love you.

But how to wrap your mind around meetings with these [strike]dummi[/strike]your beloved clients? Well, every business shark needs a calendar! And you do get one in DDS2. Just take a look.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43095044/b1de4e3f92810c065cb22d3cc31f54a8fd3c33fc.jpg[/img]

It's not that easy to cater to everyone. Each region has its preferred products. Once you get bigger and expand, you'll need employees to handle deliveries. Just select where you want them to work on the map, and leave the product for them in a deaddrop. Your people will take care of the rest and give you money once you talk with them (or invite them to the hideout). 

However, the dealers you hire will get a share of your proceeds! Yes, the life of a dealer isn't easy. At first, [b]it ain't much, but it's dishonest work[/b]. Only after working hard you can reap your rewards and live a life of luxury.

[b]Taste a bit of it in the demo - incoming December 18.[/b]
Wishlist below to not miss a thing.

notes.title: DevLog: Incoming demo and the PRODUCT *wink wink*
notes.notes:
How are you today, Dealers? Y’all ready for the upcoming demo? Good news: it’s almost here! On December 18, you’ll get a free sample of goodness to come. Make sure to play it, because this time it’s a time-limited demo. It’ll be up until January 2. 

The demo will be LONG, and it will have a lot of things we planned for the full game. In the next few days, we’ll talk about what’s in the demo, how it works, and how you can use it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43095044/6fbd53c8dff02600737ad57ae4c0cdd10b3151e6.png[/img]

Let’s start with…

[h1]THE [strike]DRU[/strike]PRODUCT![/h1]

First, the facts.

In the demo, you will find 2 types of products (there will be many more in the full game): cannabis and amphetamine. You can either buy the product to sell or prepare it yourself.

If you choose to prepare the product, you can do it at a hideout.

[h2]So how to produce pot?[/h2]
[list][*] Buy the ingredients: water, fertilizer, seeds.
[*] Plant the seeds (e.g. in a growbox) to grow the plant.
[*] Use the drier to dry the herbs.[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43095044/bc703e0e5f8f6a9ae6425d3d32edd01408c44df0.jpg[/img]
[h2]And how to make amphetamine?[/h2]
[list][*] Buy the ingredients. Different ingredients are needed depending on which recipe you choose. You can see the recipe in the cooker.
[*] Buy a cooker and a pot.
[*] Prepare the amphetamine base (amphetamine salts, according to one of three recipes).
[*] Prepare the amphetamine using the cooker.[/list]
The above is a simple recipe, you’ll come across more advanced ones as you develop your cartel in the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43095044/9d004f178b9a5ad65b5feb34528bb1514c911546.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43095044/76876481604bc0623c3fa3b60a495a235960ab44.png[/img]
However!

Making the product isn’t enough. You need to portion and pack it, too. To do it, you must have a laboratory tray, plastic bags or stretch wrap, and duct tape. 

PSA: We do not encourage you to try this at home. You will fail anyway because these are not 100% accurate production processes. This is a game. “A great game!” you might say, and we would nod with approval. But still, just a game.

Have fun! And let us know how your chef career went in the demo. We have a special place for feedback on our [url=https://discord.gg/drugdealersim]Discord[/url]. 

Remember – December 18 is the day. See ya on Isla Sombra!

We decided to push the premiere to the next year. We know you're waiting eagerly to play it, but here's the thing: we want to make the best game we can, and that takes time. We want it to be polished.

notes.title: Holy cow! Get on the road with Alaskan Road Truckers!
Massive Q&A finale!
notes.notes:
Still some more questions to go. Ready your peepers and go!

[b]Q: Will there be workshop support?[/b]
A: No planned mod support for now. We’ll let you know.

[b]Q: Can you make changes to the in-game world?[/b]
A: Yes, there are a couple of ways you can influence the world and change the environment.

[b]Q: Are there any random events/encounters?[/b]
A: Yes, there will be some, but not to a big extent.

[b]Q: Can you have a pet?[/b]
A: Yes, you can have pets in the hideouts that give you bonuses.

[b]Q: Is there a moral aspect in DDS2?[/b]
A: There is a reputation system with the game world communities and a stress system.

[b]Q: Are there any future plans for DLC/events/updates (other than patches) for DDS2?[/b]
A: No specific plans that we can share for now, but possibly.

[b]Q: Is there a way to make a soundtrack for DDS2?[/b]
A: We’ve just posted a music challenge so take a look there! And if you miss that chance, go to our Discord Server music chat and ask K. Pietras, the composer, himself!

[previewyoutube=1srzQBDVn7s;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]Q: Any chance you can add me into the game with the name "Darth Trace"? haha[/b]
A: General Kenobi?

[b]Q: Are there Easter Eggs in DDS2?[/b]
A: Wouldn’t be an Easter Egg if we spill the beans now, no?

[b]Q How many saves/profiles can you have in DDS2?[/b]
A: The cartel progress runs on one base save + backups, you can create as many cartel instances (playthroughs) as you’d like. 

[b]Q: Is there a jail system?[/b]
A: Yes, but we don’t want to spoil more details for now :)

[b]Q: Making money means being able to spend money. Is there anything new in DDS2 like buying luxury goods or prostitution that I can enjoy my daily life with the money I earn?[/b]
A: Oh yes, there are a lot more ways to spend money in the game than in the original, up to some very expensive ones. 

[b]Q: Can I not only sell drugs but also produce raw materials and build production lines?[/b]
A: Yes, the lab system is much more complex and improved.

[b]Q: Will there be a new skill or technology tree?[/b]
A: There will be unlockable perks for both playable characters as well as your cartel. 

[b]Q: Will I have black market stores or shops to sell drugs?[/b]
A: There will be some wholesale clients on the island, yes.

[b]Q: Is there an economic system with a supply-demand relationship?[/b]
A: Yes, demand for specific drugs can rise or drop as a consequence of your actions and it affects your sales and client base.

[b]Q: Can we bribe the government or even puppet a government?[/b]
A: Maybe not an entire government, but there are bribery options and some political aspects to the game, yes. 

[b]Q: In the later stages of the game, will I still be a peddler running errands and making deliveries, or can I become the boss of a drug empire?[/b]
A: You can become a boss, there is a much more complex progression than in the original.

[b]Q: Will there be hunger and thirst?[/b]
A: No, there are some environmental threats but no survival mechanism. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43095044/3f1fe922493b70d8df4d988ea0a8f250bcb0ba5d.png[/img]

[b]Q: Will you be able to find weed strains all over the map and breed them to create new strains?[/b]
A: There are a few strains available and you grow them from scratch, yes. 

[b]Q: Are the things you learn in the game applicable to real life (asking for a friend)?[/b]
A: The production systems are researched and inspired by real-life processes, but are not precise and are simplified to the game needs. 

[b]Q: Will we be able to set prices for a specific mix? Will dealers sometimes try to avoid paying?[/b]
A: You decide on what drug or mix you distribute for the specific drug demand and have some control over the pricing. 

[b]Q: Can we get a client who is a scientist (imagine) and somehow allow us to have easier access to the necessary supplies? Or maybe even sell us out?[/b]
A: Not clients, but there are world NPCs that either sell us items, byproducts and equipment or can help us unlock tech and knowledge to improve.

[b]Q: We know we will have co-op, but will we be able to create separate empires on the same map?[/b]
A: No, the game is based on cooperative PvE, all players share one cartel. 

[b]Q: How many different types of Drugs will there be?[/b]
A: We will inform you of the full list closer to the release. We are still considering some changes. 

There you have it! Brains still working after that influx of info?

notes.title: More questions answered!
notes.notes:
Been waiting? Good. So here is Q&A part 2.

[b]Q: Will you be able to switch between single player and multiplayer? If you start a multiplayer game, but then that person can’t play a session, can you play solo, and then switch back to multi when they are available?[/b]
A: Yes, you can freely migrate your progress between coop and single player sessions with various players. If the player who resigns is the host, he can share with you his save files for  use solo or host the game for new players. We put a lot of effort into making it as flexible as possible.

[b]Q: Will the Steam Deck Controller be supported in the game?[/b]
A: There are no plans for this for now. We might consider it after the full game is released. 

[b]Q: Do you plan to expand the RPG aspect (character development, decisions that affect the game world)?[/b]
A: Yes it is expanded from the original game, but I wouldn’t compare it to a regular RPG. 

[b]Q: How much bigger is it going to be from DDS1?[/b]
A: A LOT! There are multiple times larger play areas including villages, towns, and wildlands as well as water paths for boats (rivers, ocean)

[b]Q: Will it be server-based multiplayer or locally hosted?[/b]
A: We plan on doing both, but we are still planning on how to handle dedicated server support.

[b]Q: Will it be possible to play the game on a Mac?[/b]
A: No, unfortunately, Windows PC only.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43095044/2bd7fe9b2719330d1327b5d37c06daa781f334a6.png[/img]

[b]Q: In co-op, can you and your "partner" focus on different drugs?[/b]
A: Yes, you can divide the tasks between players in various ways. Production, distribution, expansion, business, questing. You make your strategy.

[b]Q: Will we be able to focus on making just one drug to base our market on for roleplaying purposes, or will we need to diversify to be sustainable?[/b]
A: Diversifying will give you much more clients and more sales, but you can scale your operation to any extent you feel comfortable. You can go through the entire game only focusing on one product if you like. 

[b]Q: Do you have people mixing for you, or do you have to do it all yourself like in DDS1?[/b]
A: NPC’s help in production and you have more options for big batch production (larger scale equipment)

[b]Q: The game will be co-op, but will we be able to be rival drug lords or will we have to team up?[/b]
A: The gameplay is a cooperative PvE. All players play in one team. 

[b]Q: I dream of seeing the work of a cook in this game, like in the movie "Breaking Bad", will there be such a system in this game? If so, I'll cry with happiness.[/b]
A: Yes, but someone has to deal with distribution. If you want to 100% focus on lab work, you’ll probably need friends or at least do the initial leg work to set up your distribution with NPC’s

[b]Q: Will there be a system to build your own house (with a lab, multiple floors)?[/b]
A: There is no building system, but there are a variety of apartments available from flats to warehouses as well as villas and houses with yards.

[b]Q: Will there be drug use animations (smoking a blunt, snorting coke, or popping an oxy)? Will I be able to take drugs like in DDS1 (with additional animations)?[/b]
A: There will be some, yes. 

[b]Q: Will there be a realistic chemistry system (ability to synthesize drugs from precursors)?[/b]
A: The production system is based on deep chemical research we did, so it is somewhat “realistic” but simplified to the game's needs so it’s not too complicated and enjoyable. 

[b]Q: Will the weed plantations be realistic?[/b]
A: As mentioned above, yes but to an extent. It is simplified.  

[b]Q: Will there be side hustles/businesses?[/b]
A: Yes, there are side quests, break-ins and other activities.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43095044/dc995fda6a992b28a99c1aa709fb05116d0ef261.png[/img]

[b]Q: How are you guys at the office handling all of our love, support, and impatience?[/b]
A: We are big boys and girls, we’re handling it <3 

[b]Q: Could we have influential people in the game to deliver drugs to? For example, having the composer of LeLeLe 2.0 represented in the game as a client and increasing our rep with him can give us access to progression events or give us additional perks?[/b]
A: There will be some, but we don’t want to spoil them.

[b]Q: Can we choose more specific amounts for the packaging instead of 1/3/5/10/etc.?[/b]
A: Yes! The packaging system is improved and more flexible.

[b]Q: Can we accidentally (or purposely) give more drugs to our clients that make them happier with us or something like that?[/b]
A: Yes.

[b]Q: Can we bribe authorities to get out of sticky situations?[/b]
A: Yes, in some cases you can.

[b]Q: Will there be achievements?[/b]
A: Steam achievements? Yes, definitely. 

[b]Q: Can you have a crew of dealers?[/b]
A: Yep! You’ll unlock this option as you progress through the game.

[b]Q: Will we have the opportunity to grow our business with a really big order like 200 kg of weed?[/b]
A: The amounts you sell and distribute highly increase while you progress. 

[b]Q: Sex update when?[/b]
A: Got the wrong game here, pal, Lust from Beyond is this way 👉 https://store.steampowered.com/app/1035120/Lust_from_Beyond/

Part 3 coming soon!

notes.title: You asked - now we answer
notes.notes:
Y’all, another Q&A is rolling in! You asked (a TON of questions, sometimes many times), and we have the answers ready. There are sooooooooooooo many questions that we had to split this post into 3 parts so we wouldn’t overload the page.

Go and enjoy!

[b]Q: Will there be DLSS support?[/b]
A: Yes, we are planning DLSS support. We are waiting to implement it in a newer version of the engine, so not sure if it will be there for the demo, but most likely for the full release.

[b]Q: Will there be a system to produce synthetic drugs? Setting up labs and buying chemicals?[/b]
A: Yes, DDS2 lab system is way more advanced than what we had in the original. All of the drugs have their production chains, base ingredients are obtained in various ways (not to spoil anything). You have control over how complex your production and distribution chain is and how many types of products you want to focus on.

[b]Q: What is Rafał's favorite color?[/b]
A: Yes.

[b]Q: What's the estimated time to complete the game (hours)?[/b]
A: It will highly vary depending on your goals and playstyle. We put much effort into making DDS2 fit for both casual and hardcore “max out” audiences that want to spend very long hours and weeks in the game. You have a lot of control over your priorities, scale of the operation, expansion range and tactics. Depending on how much you want from the game you could possibly spend anything from 15 to 100 hours in one complete playthrough. It is very hard to estimate.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43095044/443fc801959d4182993146269c69c1ec2b8cea58.png[/img]

[b]Q: How will the co-op work? Are you all equal in the group or are there leaders, distributors, and street dealers?[/b]
A: The game host is the main boss and has a few additional options, but you are mostly equal. How you divide your duties all depends on your planning. There also are NPC employees who can do some stuff for you, and balancing bonuses for smaller parties and single players.

[b]Q: What is the maximum number of people you can play with?[/b]
A: For now we plan to make the co-op for up to 3 people. This might change for the full release. The limit is both a technical and a design+balance thing to consider and we need a bit more time and polish to finalise the decision.

[b]Q: How does the save system work when playing in co-op?[/b]
A: Each game session is started by creating a new cartel. The cartel progress is saved on the host computer (or a single player PC) or dedicated server. There are also some progress elements that save locally per player. You can freely and easily migrate cartel save files between machines as well as between Co-op and single-player sessions at any point in time. Example: You can start a singleplayer session and decide to invite your friend along the way, use your save on a dedicated server to continue, or use a coop session save to continue and finish the playthrough alone.

[b]Q: Will there be an option to create a gang?[/b]
A: Creating a cartel is the basis for starting a new game session. It’s built out of both players as well as NPCs.

[b]Q: Where is Eddie ;(?[/b]
A: Eddie is one of the playable characters you can choose from as well as one of the two selectable narrators for the story. 

[b]Q: Will there be any new drugs in the game?[/b]
A: Yes, there are a few new drugs as well as new drug forms. Part of the available drugs are the same types as in the original, but each of them has a unique production chain, with multiple lab equipment types and sizes. Obtaining product is much more complex and engaging than simply unlocking and ordering.

[b]Q: Will gangs/wholesaling become more prominent?[/b]
A: There are more wholesale clients to obtain in the game, yes. You also hire NPCs to “automate” your distribution chain, so you don’t have to deal with all the clients (if you don’t want to). This way you can also focus on more wholesale deliveries, big batch production and smuggling just to supply your employees with products and collect cash.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43095044/a4ef9bbec55fbcbeca4d4f31c7bd6947d2d02d1c.png[/img]

[b]Q: Can I make my own drug and name it?[/b]
A: You can’t make “your own drug” per se, but you can make named mixes like in DDS1. You can produce all of the types of drugs available on your own tho. 

[b]Q: Will there be freedom to explore in co-op, or is there a tethered system?[/b]
A: You can free to explore wherever you like. There is no leash or distance limit system for the players. You only need to keep in mind that for listen servers (local player-hosted games) all explored areas need to be partially loaded on the server, so it may affect the host’s gameplay performance depending on his rig. 

[b]Q: Will there be any plot in the game or is it just an introduction and free play?[/b]
A: There is a full story for the cartel and an entire playthrough up till the end. There is an open ending for the cartel and a final “ending ending” for each player unlocked upon reaching the cartel ending. The main story and how you go through it will also partially adapt and evolve depending on your choices, priorities and playstyle.

[b]Q: Will you be able to place drugs in marked zones like Eddie did in DDS1, or just sell from hand to hand?[/b]
A: Yes, you can hire your own NPC dealers that you supply by dead drops. You start the game as a “man on the ground” but can progress all the way up to only managing large-scale operations and using minions to do most of the leg work for you. 

[b]Q: Will we be able to get dyes to make custom colored drugs?[/b]
A: There are no dyes, but we’ll think about that. There are multiple color coding and custom naming features for organizing your gameplay tho. You can name employees, hideouts, containers, boats, organise substance storage and more. 

[b]Q: Will you be able to create a sub-network of NPC dealers in single-player mode, e.g. have NPCs distribute your stuff or collect resources?[/b]
A: Yes, that’s exactly how it works. You can hire NPC’s for dealers as well as other tasks and distribution.

[b]Q: Was the playtest a full release or a beta?[/b]
A: The playtest is still in progress and considers the full game, but we are still working on some of the content, balance and mechanics. The community testers help us with finding issues, discuss features and polishing the balance of the whole game. 

[b]Q: Will there be a gang reputation?[/b]
A: Yes, you have a reputation to maintain with the game world and it has a much wider impact on the gameplay than in DDS1.

notes.title: More questions answered! Q&A part 2
notes.notes:
For those of you who might have missed it – we have coop! 

It’s huge news, so let’s hear Big Boss talk about it once again.

[previewyoutube=p_AXdpv1qHI;full][/previewyoutube]

We’ve collected your questions and already answered half of them in [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1708850/view/3717199657478810266?l=english]the previous post[/url]. And now, ready for MORE INFO? Let’s dive in! (Also psst, check the end of the post too)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43095044/0c04bc04b3a48c4ebed8204845e0dd95367e88d0.png[/img]
[b]Q:[/b] Can we get more voiceovers for NPCs?
[b]A:[/b] As DDS2 has a much higher budget, yes, there will be more voiceovers and overall a much, much more alive environment overall.

[b]Q:[/b] If I am not a host of the session, when I leave the game, what progress will I have saved?
[b]A:[/b] You will save over your individual character progress as well as host-relative cartel progress. You'll be able to transfer character progress between cartels if the cartel owner allows it.

The exact specifics are still in development and tweaking tho.

[b]Q: [/b]Can you create a server so if the original host is not playing, the other friend can play?
[b]A:[/b] Yes, we are working on delivering a maximally flexible solution. We will give more details on that later.

[b]Q:[/b] Will we have vehicles (like cars or boats)?
[b]A:[/b] Yes, there are cars and boats in the game. It is not a fully fletched free driving system like GTA or so, but you'll need a vehicle to travel around the island as it is a significantly larger world than DDS1. The vehicles use roads, rivers and the open sea to travel between towns and villages.

You'll use them for far travel, smuggling items and dope or exfiling from locations when it gets hot. More on that later

[b]Q:[/b] Are there any plans for expanding upon mixing/lab work? Anything from acquiring a product to processing it further than what exists in DDS1?
[b]A:[/b] The lab and hideout system and drug logistics/production/processing are significantly improved in comparison to DDS1. You will have control over the complexity of your production, stimulate drug demand and obtain products and various chemicals and ingredients in various ways.

That includes multiple-step production, processing, buying, smuggling and stealing. You will be able to decide on the strategy, complexity and variety of your offer and choose from ways of acquiring products that fit your cartel’s financial expectations.

[b]Q:[/b] Can you wholesale your drugs?
[b]A:[/b] Yes, there will be mid and late-game wholesale buyers, but you also hire NPCs to your hierarchy to deal with the low-level distribution so you can focus on the higher scale of the entire operation.

[b]Q:[/b] Will there be shops to buy stuff like in the first game or do you have to find it (bags, additives etc.)?
[b]A:[/b] Yes there are multiple shops and NPCs to buy things from, but also many other ways of acquiring items and chemicals like looting, stealing, crafting and environment exploration.

[b]Q:[/b] Can I cook meth in DDS2 by myself?
[b]A:[/b] Yes, Walter. Yes, you can.

[b]Q:[/b] Will there be a deep water culture?
[b]A:[/b] We haven't planned DWC but might include it. There are a few ways for weed farming planned with different types of equipment and setups.

[b]Q:[/b] Can you add more floors to the apartments? Can we use an elevator?
[b]A:[/b] Yes, the apartments will have much more variety in size, floors as well as being indoor, outdoor or mixed. More on that later.

[b]Q:[/b] Will there be a favela on the island? If yes, will you be able to take it over?
[b]A:[/b] Yes, there are different types of towns and villages on the island, including favelas. Not sure what you mean by "take over" but you will surely grow your influence in the towns.

[b]Q:[/b] What about bribing the police and making deals with other cartels?
[b]A:[/b] There will be bribing of NPCs, including the police. There are also other criminal organisations in the game, but we'll share more about that later.

[b]Q:[/b] Will there be Steam Workshop?
[b]A:[/b] We are not planning workshop or mod support for now, but planning to include tools and settings to customise the gameplay to your liking.

[b]Q:[/b] Will there be voiceovers in different languages?
[b]A: [/b]The NPCs in the world will use different languages, but assuming you are asking about game localization - unfortunately not. Only UI + subtitles will have translations.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43095044/291b83b3133d54aaf1e42c68e34d5a9a294cc72b.png[/img]

Is your curiosity satisfied for the moment, dealers? Let us know if you wanna know more!

Also! Do you know what’s happening this Sunday? It’s the 3-year anniversary of DDS1! We have some things coming to celebrate, so keep your eyes peeled for new posts. 👀

notes.title: We have answers for you!
notes.notes:
Just as we suspected, you had around a bazillion questions after the last video we released. So many, in fact, that we had to split this Q&A session in half. So, let’s see how Big Boss Rafal ™ answered them!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43095044/87946bd86cdb40ccd2e9fd2eba1604cfbf2b2a49.png[/img]
[b]Question:[/b] Will there be guns or any other weapons?
[b]Answer:[/b] As we stated earlier, there will be no guns and shooting mechanics in Drug Dealer Simulator. We are considering adding some specific and limited forms of self-defence and violence to DDS2, but this is not a promise. It's still WIP.

[b]Q:[/b] What about bribing the police and making deals with other cartels?
[b]A:[/b] There will be bribing of NPCs, including the police. There are also other criminal organisations in the game, but we'll share more on that later.

[b]Q:[/b] Will police patrols and checks be as repetitive as in DDS1?
[b]A:[/b] No, we are improving the system in a few ways as well as adding a few types of opponents instead of just one. We will share more info when we have them more polished.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43095044/54e124375c2dd3519d88ca71911d122dd57c8266.png[/img]

[b]Q:[/b] Can you decide on the hierarchy in your cartel?
[b]A:[/b] Yes, you hire NPC's met and unlocked during gameplay. You either put them in the sales hierarchy to manage sales for you or assign them different tasks. You can also share responsibilities with other players in coop mode, obviously.

[b]Q:[/b] Will there be cartel wars or cartel politics?
[b]A:[/b] No "wars" per se, as we do not include combat in the game, but there will be a decent share of roleplay and politics in the gameplay and main storyline.

[b]Q:[/b] Will we be able to beta test DDS2?
[b]A:[/b] We are not sure about a beta, but it's possible. We do not have any specific on that yet. Stay tuned!

[b]Q:[/b] Will there be a demo?
[b]A:[/b] There is a demo in plans, but we don't have any specific to share yet. Stay tuned!

[b]Q:[/b] Can we customize our character?
[b]A:[/b] There will be two default story characters to choose from or a custom one to create. We will include a basic character creator. Also - the game has exchangeable clothes which change your looks as well as stats and inventory.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43095044/5c0433cb29303ca659bbf700a6f3c769f4823fa2.png[/img]

[b]Q:[/b] Will we be able to choose our character in co-op or will we both be playing as Eddie?
[b]A:[/b] You will be able to choose from two default story characters and a custom character of your own.

[b]Q:[/b] Will the game be easier with more people joining in from coop or does it not affect it whatsoever?
[b]A:[/b] It is somewhat easier on one hand, but with more players, we also scale up the gameplay. Every player will have their own requirements for items, tools, clothes, housing and consumables. This means more work, more cash, more questing and exploring. There is both cartel progression as well as individual progression.

[b]Q:[/b] Is there a limit of people being able to join in?
[b]A:[/b] There must be some limit, but we have not yet decided on the exact number. Many factors need to be considered when making this decision (hosting, balance, optimization and more). We will decide on that when we have the mechanical core, netcode and balance fully finished. The code base is designed to handle multiplier players, but we need a bit more work done to make the final decision.

[b]Q:[/b] So traditionally in single player if you got arrested it would skip your night in jail, with co-op will the other player literally have to wait for their buddy who got caught to be set free while they are stuck in a jail cell?
[b]A:[/b] We have w new system in place, without the time skip that fits both single-player and coop, but being honest - I just don't want to spoil it yet :) I think you'll really like it tho.

[b]Q:[/b] Will you be able to play against each other in a PvP mode?
[b]A:[/b] No, there will be no competitive PvP mode. The game is based around PvE cooperation and progressing your cartel together, with a common goal.

[b]Q:[/b] If your partner gets arrested can you break them out or bribe the police to release them?
[b]A:[/b] We have a new interesting system for handling arrests for both single player and coop, but we will share more details in the future :) It will be very unique from DDS1.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43095044/291b83b3133d54aaf1e42c68e34d5a9a294cc72b.png[/img]

Part 2 coming soon, stay tuned!

notes.title: COOP – CONFIRMED
notes.notes:
Hi there, dealers! Ready for the beans?

And oh boy, do we have news for you. 

We’ve seen some of you already picking up on clues, hints, and a stray tag too. And yes. [b]Drug Dealer Simulator 2 features coop – CONFIRMED. [/b]

Here’s a word from the big boss Rafal. Let’s hear what he has to say.

[previewyoutube=p_AXdpv1qHI;full][/previewyoutube]

[i]When planning Drug Dealer Simulator 2, we knew we needed something more, something that will be “higher level” so to speak. It was important to keep the heart and soul of the original gameplay loop, but at the same time improve and expand it on many levels. Having the new game architecture set up from the ground up, with all the gathered experience – we had the perfect opportunity to introduce coop to the project.

I believe that playing games in coop is the future. Experiencing everything the game has to offer on another level. In a way, you keep the immersive intimacy of a single-player game but live the adventure together with your friends. Running your own cartel with companions with the new, expanded world and features is in my opinion a real game-changer for the franchise.

Obviously, the player will be able to choose if he wants to dominate the Island alone in a single-player playthrough, start his journey with friends or maybe start solo and invite members on the way. We are working on delivering a flexible drop-in drop-out system. You set up your cartel, you’re the boss, others may join or leave when you feel like it, it’s all up to you.

Even now with a few core mechanics still in development, we are having lots of fun playtesting the game together. From what we have now and where this is going - it will be so much more than JUST a sequel…[/i]

***

So there, the beans have been spilt!

We’re sure you have about a bazillion questions right now. Ask them all in the comments to this post, and we will collect them and answer to the best of our ability. Fire away!

[b]Will the Unreal Engine 5 graphics be better?[/b]

Yes, and significantly so! Not just because of better effects, lighting etc., but in general because of the visual direction.

In DDS1, I remember having a large amount of trouble trying to lace weed with other drugs. Is there a likelihood of this being easier to accomplish in DDS2?

The drug/substance production and processing system is highly improved. It is more complex and more user-friendly at the same time. We rethought the workstations and their issues from the first game, analyzed community playthroughs and setups and made significant improvements.

[b]Will DDS2 be more varied?[/b]

Yes, we learned that our community spends long hours playing DDS and adapted the gameplay. It evolves in time and gives you more options to engage in fresh activities.

[b]Will we also get to use chemicals for drug production, and not only grow stuff?[/b]

Yes, we redesigned many aspects of the lab configuration, some drugs you will be able to buy, others you'll need to produce out of other substances that you'll obtain in different ways. You will also have more control over your offer, inventory and stimulating demand for your preferred playstyle.

[b]Can we have a lab that analyzes the drugs you or your competitors made and see how toxic, addictive etc. it is?[/b]

Yes, there will be special lab equipment for mixing, purification and analyzing obtained substances for purity and contents/contamination.

[b]Why is a sequel in the works when the final update for the predecessor is not yet out? Also, you mentioned that DDS is at its limits. Why don’t these limits apply to a sequel in a different setting?[/b]

The production of the base for DDS2 started with a separate team and now as we finish up the first part we can jump fully into the second one. Also, the limitations were not with the creative vision, but with the technical side of DDS1. Read into the previous FAQ, Rafal had already talked about it there.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43095044/eea08668aef76b99562401b948f163116166fdb9.jpg[/img]

[b]Will there be workshop support?[/b]

We decided not to implement mod support for DDS1. As for DDS2 the matter is being discussed.

[b]Will there be some potential randomized/dynamic events?[/b]

We’re thinking about how to approach this, but we’d rather not talk about it until we have it all worked out. 

[b]Will players who bought DDS1 get a discount for DDS2?[/b]

Our publisher Movie Games creates the pricing policy for their games. They usually offer ‘complete-the-set’ bundles upon release, where the owners of their other games will be able to save extra money on the newly released game. So, in short, yes, you can expect some extra savings if you own DDS1.

[b]What’s the plan for DDS2 updates?[/b]

We'll get back to this when the core and base game is ready. We've designed the technical core much better for much easier support and expansion but don't have a specific post-release plan in mind yet.

Alright! This should cover most of the stuff that you’ve been asking about. If you want to discuss something further, join our [url=https://discord.gg/b6nkeQgF]Discord[/url] or follow our [url=https://twitter.com/DDSSimulator]Twitter[/url] or [url=https://www.facebook.com/DDSSimulator/]Facebook[/url]. As for Steam, we’ll be back with DDS1 Endgame update, and also some production news or diaries about DDS2. 

Follow us, wishlist the game, and stay in touch!

notes.title: FAQ: sequel, update, behind the scenes & more
notes.notes:
Hey everyone! 

Rafal here, the game director of DDS1 and 2. I’m floored by the amount of feedback we got from you regarding both games after we announced part 2. First of all, thanks for the effort you took to respond. I’d like to address as many issues that you’ve raised as possible, and together with Movie Games we figured that it’ll be best to prepare a proper FAQ. 

We’ll combine questions about both games here, because you usually asked about the development process, and how one game affects the other.  Well, find out below. :) 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43095044/bf999855604c38f6b176cf7772aca20d70969e52.png[/img]

You can read this FAQ both on the DDS1 and DDS2 Steam page.

Frequently Asked Questions

[b]1. So is DDS2 really a prequel?[/b]

Indeed, it is a prequel. You will experience Eddie's rise to the high cartel ranks at Isla Sombra. In a way - you write his story. You do not need to know the events of DDS1 to enjoy DDS2.

We wanted to keep the core of DDS1 heart and gameplay while giving the game its own identity, thus the new setting. We decided that Eddie's backstory will be perfect for both introducing a fresh setting as well as new gameplay challenges by running the business "the old way".

I think that we all like Eddie and that he deserves his own larger chunk of the story, more than he was given in part 1. I also believe Eddie’s popularity is in huge part due to Christopher Neal’s fantastic performance, and I’m happy to confirm that Chris will narrate DDS2. 

[b]2. Will DDS2 get updates? How frequently?[/b]

Taking our experiences as well as mistakes from the first part, we want to deliver DDS2 as a larger, much more full and polished experience at premiere point. Aside from that the game will still get support as long as it will need it. Expansions might also come, but time will tell.

[b]3. Does DDS2 mean you’re dropping DDS1?[/b] 

Not dropping. Completing. We want Endgame to be the final update that ties up all the loose ends and adds much more stuff for you to play with. We’ve been supporting DDS and publishing free updates for 2 years. It’s time to move on, because we’ve reached the limit of what we can do with the DDS technical framework.

This being the last content update does not mean end of support though. We will still be there to fix issues and bugs as far as the game core allows us to. We are also including a lot of requested QoL changes with the Endgame patch.

[b]4. What about guns and the stuff you showed in the first DDS1 trailer?[/b]

Yes, that trailer is haunting us to this day. All I can say is that neither myself nor Movie Games would publish this trailer today. So what happened?

Well, first of all - the original DDS1 announcement was made during a very early stage of production, when the game was a vision in prototyping - if I may call it that way. As we dug deeper into assembling the core gameplay, we came to realize that some of the features we envisioned in the game either won't actually work well for the gameplay or quite simply - we won't be able to make them. At least not well enough for us to be acceptable.

First of all - that is a normal part of the game development process, but - as a fairly inexperienced developer at that time - I wasn't able to fully foresee it. Secondly, the guns in the trailer (as one of the examples) were more of a "cinematic enhancement", and, collectively, we wrongly assumed that they won't be treated as a promised gameplay feature. This was a wrong assumption. We understand that now. 

We can't turn back time, but we sure can - and did - learn from our mistakes. Additionally, shooting - as fun as it may sound in theory - would ruin the balance and low-profile playstyle of DDS also introducing numerous additional issues we were not up for solving. That is why we scrapped the idea in early stages. 

I know and understand that some of you felt cheated by that and I am truly sorry. We are all just people and make mistakes. Now, as we know the IP much better and learned from our mistakes - we are able to have more control over what the end form of our game will be. DDS2 is a different story and I'm convinced you'll love it, just as we do. No guns tho... as we already established :)

[b]5. Will all the things from the DDS2 trailer be in the game, or will it be a DDS1 deja vu?[/b]

The DDS1 announcement was a huge lesson for everyone involved. We made sure to not include anything in the DDS2 trailer that would not appear in the game. I mean, it would’ve been really stupid of us to repeat the same mistake, right? 

The DDS2 trailer is obviously cinematic but uses a lot of actual in-game assets and was made much further into prototyping the gameplay. We still have a lot of work ahead, but the core gameplay is set and well thought through. All the shown scenes have their "in-game relatives". The time for a gameplay reveal, and footage of how exactly we combined these elements in the game itself, will come when we are ready to show them.

Surely - some minor changes might and probably will come. In the end, all that matters is the good of the game as a whole, but what we've shown you are core elements of the actual gameplay. There is also more to it, but we leave the best for last. :)

[previewyoutube=S9dn2BS7yDU;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]6. So will DDS2 have all the stuff the fans have been wanting?[/b]

Surely not ALL, as there are a lot of dreams and ideas out there, but in the second installment we did our best to combine our own vision, and what is best in DDS1, with all the knowledge and ideas we took from the community. We want it to be a much better version of the original. In short we're adding everything that is reasonable and doable while maintaining our core vision.

There is a much larger world with more to do, better AI, way better and more complex cartel progress (from street level to boss) and much more engaging drug production/distribution system. The player has more control over his strategies, assortment and playstyle. We want it to fit the huge engagement and commitment of the game's community which we did not expect initially for DDS1. Also - there are a few really big and great features that we'll announce if we are fully certain we have control over. But more on that will come later.

Bottom line: We expanded DDS1 to the limits of the original technical core, added what made sense but a lot of it was just much better to save for a fresh, better designed from scratch game, made with larger experience and MUCH newer technology. Stay tuned for more info on what's to come.

[b]7. Why is the DDS1 update taking so long?[/b]

First things first - it's a big update. It introduces a couple of new mechanics as well as an endgame questline. We are also adding many community requested quality-of-life improvements and features, Steam Achievements and more as well as fixing lots of old bugs. That alone is a lot of testing, polishing as well as balancing with the new features in the loop.

Additionally - DDS1 expanding and changing is very time consuming and complicated. First - as we established in earlier questions - its technical core is simply badly made in various ways and cannot be fully remade or fixed. Fixing issues brings new issues, reworks break game files, unchangeable modules have to be worked around and so on. Maintaining the stability of saved games on various levels of progress is a big part of it too. Obviously with that in mind we have to quadruple check different save files, fresh playthroughs, late game playthroughs and so on with EACH iteration. 

Again - that's a huge part why we decided to start fresh and incorporate part of our plan for the "perfect DDS" in a new game which is DDS2. Trust me - that's really the best way to go and you won't be disappointed. :)

[b]8. Did DDS2 slow the development of the update?[/b]

Only partially, for most of the time DDS2 was prototyped and developed by an additional group of people, but under our guidance - for obvious reasons. Now the time has come for us to jump in fully to maximize DDS2 experience and it is time to put the DDS1 expansion to a proper end.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43095044/c672e03dd9add8ddd367fd7be69ff51505e98465.png[/img]

[b]9. DDS on consoles[/b]

We’ve been trying to make it happen for a long time, but here’s something you might not know. Console platform owners have to approve your game on their platform. They have much, much stricter content rules than Steam, and in general they don’t want “problematic” games. Adult games won’t ever come out on consoles. And when you have a game where you distribute drugs and use them, it is extremely difficult to convince the platforms to put it next to cute purple dragons and bandicoots.

You can say: but what about game X or Y? It has drugs and it’s on consoles! Yes, but usually drugs are just a minor part of these titles, or they’re stigmatized and portrayed as bad. This kinda isn’t the case with DDS. 

So: we’ll keep trying to make it happen, but I wouldn’t hold my breath. It’s not because of the lack of will. It’s because we made a game called Drug Dealer Simulator. :) If you want DDS on consoles, maybe it would be best to tell this to PlayStation or Xbox. When they see a lot of people voicing it, they might reconsider.

[b]10. Will there be controller support for DDS1 and DDS2?[/b]

Yes, we redesigned the input complexity and UI of the original, and we are trying to adapt it for gamepads. We also added features like radial menus and so on for making the interface as clean and friendly as possible.

[b]11. What engine will DDS2 run on?[/b]

Unreal Engine 5. Currently it's the only reasonable choice. :)

[b]12. Will there be Steam Deck support for DDS2?[/b]

There is Steam Deck support for DDS1, so I can’t see why not. We would sure want it to run on the Deck, but who knows what future holds.

[b]13. Will there be an OST for DDS2?[/b]

Yes, we are making some awesome OST for the game and will make it available to you outside the game as well. Maybe besides some licensed songs that we won't have control over.

[b]14. Will there be a fleshed-out gang hierarchy in DDS2?[/b]

Yes, the gang hierarchy in DDS2 is much more complex. You will be able to assign various tasks to your minions as well as assign clients to dealers to let you focus on more high-level business and more.

[b]15. Will there be a demo or a beta?[/b]

Movie Games releases demos for most of their games and the plan is to have one for DDS2 as well. We will inform you when it might drop. In the meantime, stay tuned for Discord and Steam announcements as we might start a closed early alpha testing stage for the community at one point. No promises yet though.

Alright! 

I think that covers all of the repeatedly asked questions. If you didn’t get a reply to yours, sorry about that. Comment below and the team will do their best to respond. 

Thanks for sticking with us, wishlist and follow the game to support us. See you in Endgame in November, and on Isla Sombra next year!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1708850/Drug_Dealer_Simulator_2/
